clue.text: Its subject: in messy warfare, male lost

definitions.text: Its subject: in messy warfare, male lost

indicators.note: a messy heap is jumbled up, so the letters of the two following phrases are thrown together and rearranged

explanation.surface: A summary of a war novel's plot: a man lost amid the chaos of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' scrambles WARFARE plus MALELOST, fifteen letters. The whole clue also describes Hemingway's novel, whose hero is lost in the confusion of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's novel follows an American ambulance officer through the chaos of the Italian front, a man adrift in a messy war.

clue.text: Court case: what the Master of the Rolls may bring into it?

indicators.note: the item brought is placed into the word just given for case

parts.note: a case heard in court is a trial

parts.words: what the Master of the Rolls may bring
parts.note: jokingly, a master of bread rolls is a baker, who would bring a bun

explanation.surface: A legal query: what would a senior English judge bring into a court case?
explanation.walkthrough: The Master of the Rolls is a senior English judge; here read literally as an expert in bread rolls, a baker, who brings a BUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body appointed to judge disputes, a kind of court.

clue.text: Chew meal, having changed starter

indicators.note: the first letter of the meal word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: Eating a meal after changing the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having changed starter' swaps the L of LUNCH for M; 'starter' looks like a first course but means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To munch is to chew steadily and noisily.

clue.text: Country man dropped rope securing article

parts.note: a paratrooper, or para, is a soldier dropped by parachute

indicators.note: the rope word holds the article fast inside it

parts.note: a guy is a rope that holds a tent or mast steady
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A man dropped a rope that was holding some item in place.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a man letting go of a rope, but 'man dropped' is one unit: a soldier dropped by parachute.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraguay is a landlocked nation in South America.

clue.text: A number entered here — vital to move quietly

parts.note: key means vital or crucial
to pad is to walk softly

explanation.surface: Instructions for someone entering a code: it is vital to move quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A keypad is a small panel of buttons on which digits such as a PIN are typed.

clue.text: Torn material valued

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric
rated means assessed or valued

explanation.surface: Some ripped fabric that was once prized.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerated describes flesh or cloth ripped or gashed.

clue.text: Opening for visitor at last not initially residing in Berlin

definitions.note: the songwriter's full name ends in Berlin, so the first name sits in front of it

indicators.note: the trimmed residing word opens up to make room for the visitor's last letter
the first letter of the synonym for residing is dropped

parts.note: living somewhere means residing there

indicators.note: the final letter of visitor is taken

explanation.surface: A visitor staying in Berlin, finally given an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVING loses its first letter ('not initially') to give IVING, which opens for R, the last of visitor. The definition points to the composer Irving Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin was the American songwriter, so this first name comes before Berlin.

clue.text: Restored health, but on borrowed time again?

definitions.meaning: a fresh burst of energy and vigour after a decline
read literally, a lease is time borrowed on property, and a new one means borrowing again

explanation.surface: Someone recovered from illness, but perhaps only on borrowed time once more.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a renewed period of vitality, and literally a renewed tenancy.

clue.text: Blessed with strength to catch fish

indicators.note: the strength word surrounds the fish as a net would catch it

parts.note: a forte is someone's strong point
tuna is a large sea fish

explanation.surface: An angler lucky enough to have the strength to land a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortunate means lucky, favoured, as if blessed.

clue.text: Batty about following a high priest

indicators.note: the reversed name comes after the letter a
about signals turning the first name back to front

parts.note: Nora Batty is a character in the long-running BBC sitcom Last of the Summer Wine

explanation.surface: Someone crazy, chasing after a senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batty' looks like 'mad' but is the surname of Nora Batty, a wrinkled-stockinged character in the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine; 'about' turns NORA into ARON.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Moses' brother was the first high priest of the Israelites.

clue.text: Angry young man briefly accompanied returning book

indicators.note: the last letter of the rebel word is cut short

parts.note: a rebel is an angry young man

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: acc. is the abbreviation for accompanied, used in music

explanation.surface: An angry youth with a companion takes back a library book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts REBEL to REBE; ACC (accompanied) is turned back by 'returning' to give CCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's novel is a famous Gothic book.

clue.text: Sneak look at conductor ignoring new duo playing

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the letter for new

parts.note: André Previn was a famous conductor

indicators.note: playing suggests the pair's letters are played around with

parts.note: we, two people together, can be a duo

explanation.surface: A sneak look at a conductor performing with a pair but not a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops N from PREVIN; 'playing' turns WE into EW.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview is an advance showing, a sneak look before release.

clue.text: Petulant refusal is the custom

definitions.meaning: a sulky 'will not', as in a child's contraction

explanation.surface: Saying no petulantly is the usual thing.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means habit; as a contraction it is a sulky 'will not'.

clue.text: In court, argue against jail in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: quod is slang for jail and wrangle means argue; against means next to

explanation.surface: A lawyer in court arguing against a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In court' looks like the law-court setting but 'court' is the definition. QUOD, British slang for prison, beside WRANGLE (argue) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrangle is a courtyard enclosed by buildings, as in a college.

clue.text: England almost besotted with it, a cold dish

indicators.note: besotted means drunk or infatuated, so the letters stagger into a new order
the last letter of England is dropped

explanation.surface: England is nearly infatuated with some cold food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts England to ENGLAN; 'besotted' rearranges ENGLAN, IT and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Galantine is boned meat or poultry pressed and served cold in its jelly.

clue.text: Buy a three-pound mix that soothes infant

indicators.note: a mix blends things, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, so three pounds gives three Ls

explanation.surface: A shopping tip: buy a three-pound blend that calms a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a gentle song sung to send a baby to sleep.

clue.text: GP moves cautiously and cleans out bed

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor, abbreviated Dr
to edge is to move slowly and carefully

explanation.surface: A family doctor creeps carefully and changes a patient's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a riverbed, not a hospital bed; GP is a British family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging scoops mud and silt from the bottom of a river or harbour.

clue.text: In a city (not London) is nothing totally unimportant

indicators.note: the following letters go in the shortened city name
not means the word London is removed

parts.note: Londonderry is a city in Northern Ireland
taken as written
taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Somewhere outside London, nothing matters at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Londonderry without London leaves DERRY, the city's other name in Northern Ireland; IS and O go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A derisory amount is so small as to be laughable, utterly insignificant.

clue.text: Sort of rate boy's bad behaviour

parts.note: the going rate is the usual price
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Rating a youngster's misbehaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are dubious or improper activities.

clue.text: Feeble commercial ban a few accept

indicators.note: the number takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: three is a few
an ad is a commercial
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A weak advert ban that a handful of people go along with.
explanation.definitionFit: A threadbare argument is thin and weak, like worn cloth.

clue.text: Free, led to crack puzzle

parts.note: to rid is to free

indicators.note: cracking something breaks it apart, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Released, someone was led to solve a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question.

clue.text: Deprived, be confident judge may intervene

indicators.note: the judge comes between the letters of the confidence word

parts.note: to bet on something is to be confident of it
a ref, referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: Someone stripped of something, sure that a judge will step in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means having lost something, deprived of it.

clue.text: Greeting government agency circular

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
O is round, circular in shape

explanation.surface: A US agency sends out a circular welcoming people.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for hello or goodbye, used informally in English.

clue.text: Trim end of toe in waders

parts.note: to snip is to cut or trim

indicators.note: the last letter of toe is taken

explanation.surface: Cutting a toenail while wearing fishing waders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waders' looks like rubber boots but means wading birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Snipe are long-billed wading birds, the plural the same as the singular.

clue.text: I hear someone coming to check

definitions.text: I hear someone coming to check

parts.words: I hear someone coming to check
parts.note: in Latin audio means I hear, and the derived word names a listener as well as an inspector of accounts who comes to check

explanation.surface: Footsteps: an inspector is on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Latin 'audire', to hear, so it once meant a listener; today it is the person who checks the books.
explanation.definitionFit: This person examines an organisation's financial records, and the Latin root means a hearer.

clue.text: Country roads twisting, say, near the middle

indicators.note: the example letters sit close to the centre of the shuffled road word
twisting signals the road word's letters are wound into a new order

parts.note: lanes are small roads
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Country lanes winding near the centre of somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' rearranges LANES into SENAL; EG goes into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a West African nation.

clue.text: Fruit needing flood regularly eaten by half of us?

indicators.note: the alternate letters go inside the word for half of us

parts.note: men make up roughly half of humanity

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of flood

explanation.surface: Fruit that needs watering, which half of us eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks L and O from fLoOd; they go inside MEN, half of us humans.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large juicy fruit.

clue.text: Unlikely to go up, if turned over and put down

indicators.note: turned over means the little word if is read backwards

parts.note: a reproof is a rebuke, a put-down

explanation.surface: A rebuke that, if reversed, would not be lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up' looks like rising but means go up in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fireproof will not burn, so it will not go up in flames.
